name: Seudati
note: An Acehnese group dance accompanied by verse and body percussion.

name: Busana adat Paksian
note: The paksian crown completes women’s ceremonial attire in Bangka Belitung.

name: Busana adat Rejang
note: Rejang bridal clothing includes richly decorated garments and ceremonial jewelry.

name: Busana tenun Baduy
note: Baduy communities wear handwoven clothing with styles that differ between Inner and Outer Baduy.

name: Busana adat Bili’u
note: Gorontalo brides wear Bili’u with elaborate ornaments and a distinctive headdress.

name: Tengkuluk
note: Women in Jambi Malay communities fold cloth into distinctive head coverings.

name: Kebaya Sunda
note: A Sundanese blouse typically worn with a batik skirt and a shawl.

name: Soto Lamongan
note: Lamongan’s chicken soup is known for its savory koya topping.

name: Tanjidor
note: A Betawi ensemble featuring wind instruments and percussion for community celebrations.

name: Pengkang
note: These triangular sticky-rice parcels contain dried shrimp and are grilled in banana leaves.

name: Nasi bekepor
note: This Kutai rice dish is cooked with spices and traditionally served with several accompaniments.

name: Mie tarempa
note: Originating in Tarempa, Anambas, these spiced noodles are commonly served with fish.

name: Babaju kun galung pacinan
note: This Banjar wedding style combines Chinese and Middle Eastern influences.

name: Juhu singkah
note: Young rattan shoots are cooked in broth, often with freshwater fish and sour eggplant.

name: Busana laki-laki Sapei Sapaq
note: This Kenyah men’s ensemble features a specially shaped garment decorated with patterned beadwork.

name: Kopiah emas
note: This metallic ceremonial cap is worn mainly by men in Lampung.

name: Kebaya dansa
note: In Ambon dress traditions, this round-necked shirt is worn by men at festivities.

name: Kimun Gia
note: The consort’s ensemble combines a white satin kebaya, songket cloth and a red shawl.

name: Pegon Sasak
note: Sasak men in Lombok pair a closed jacket with songket cloth for customary occasions.

name: Songke Manggarai
note: Manggarai songke is a predominantly black patterned cloth worn like a sarong.

name: Pelengkap anyaman pegunungan: noken
note: In Wamena, noken bags are worn with the strap over the head to carry daily necessities.

name: Busana adat Arfak: maya
note: Male Tumbu Tanah dancers traditionally wear a maya loincloth made from dried bark.

name: Busana upacara Kamoro: Mbiikao
note: In Mimika, Mbiikao masks have a rattan framework and a sheath of sago-leaf fibres.

name: Baju kurung cekak musang
note: This Malay men’s shirt has a standing collar and is worn with trousers and a waist cloth.

name: Laku tepu Sangihe
note: Sangihe ceremonial dress is traditionally made with kofo banana fibre.

name: Busana Bundo Kanduang
note: This Minangkabau women’s ensemble includes a loose blouse and a distinctive head covering.

name: Busana adat Buton
note: Buton ceremonial clothing includes kombowa, a short-sleeved blouse.

name: Tari Balumpa
note: A welcoming dance from Wakatobi.

name: Pembuatan kapal pinisi
note: South Sulawesi shipwrights pass down skills for building wooden sailing vessels.

name: Sayyang Pattudduq
note: In this Mandar tradition, trained horses move to musical rhythms.

name: Tari Tanggai
note: Graceful gestures and ornate local dress honor arriving guests.

name: Tari Pamonte
note: Kaili women perform a dance inspired by the activities of the rice harvest.

name: Sigale-gale
note: This articulated wooden puppet belongs to Batak Toba performance traditions.
